by_task.when: Illinois law applies and the asset is owned personal property.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) as an independent general-property alternative and include it even when another subsection more specifically describes the asset; its $4,000 limit caps value rather than eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply this personal-property alternative to real property, and do not omit it merely because a specific tools-of-trade or health-aid exemption also applies.

by_task.when: Illinois law applies and the asset is owned personal property.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently of every specific exemption and assign the lesser of the asset's value and $4,000.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it to real property, aggregate different assets, or displace a separately applicable specific exemption.

operations.rationale: In both EC and EV for source 149, the parent and empty control returned only the specific tools and health-aid provisions, while the released targets also contained § 5/12-1001(b) for each asset. This repairs the omitted independent general-property alternative without changing the correctly selected specific provisions.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an estate asset is being evaluated.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) for every kind of property as a separate alternative, including property also covered by a category-specific federal exemption.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat a category-specific exemption as excluding the wildcard, and do not add it where the supplied allowable jurisdictions exclude federal exemptions.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an estate asset is being evaluated.
by_task.procedure: For 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), calculate the independent claim as the lesser of the asset value and $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1); when no residence uses that amount in the independent evaluation, the ceiling is $15,425.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not aggregate allocations across assets, displace other applicable alternatives, or assume unused homestead capacity when the facts show it has been consumed.

operations.rationale: The parent repeatedly omitted § 522(d)(5): from every asset in EC sources 153–156 and from the corresponding EV alternatives, including assets with no other federal category. The targets consistently require the wildcard independently; source 155 EV also supplies the supported $15,425 ceiling when the homestead amount is unused.

by_task.when: Oregon law applies and the asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) as an independent alternative even when the asset also fits a specific Oregon exemption.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply it to real property or treat its $400 limit as a condition that makes a more valuable item ineligible.

by_task.when: Oregon law applies and the asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: For the independent Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) alternative, assign the lesser of the asset's value and $400.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not aggregate different assets or omit separately applicable Oregon exemptions.

operations.rationale: For source 153, the parent omitted § 18.345(1)(p) from both assets in EC and EV because it treated the specific household-goods provision as exclusive. The target includes both alternatives and caps the general personal-property claim at $400.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania law applies to property of the judgment debtor.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 as an independent alternative for property of any category and include it alongside any specific Pennsylvania or federal exemption.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not restrict § 8123 to cash, and do not use its $300 limit as an eligibility test for property worth more than $300.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania law applies to property of the judgment debtor.
by_task.procedure: For the independent 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 alternative, assign the lesser of the property's value and $300.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not aggregate assets, replace a specific exemption, or exclude tangible property merely because the statute is titled a monetary exemption.

operations.rationale: The parent incorrectly reasoned that § 8123 applied only to money. It consequently omitted that alternative throughout source 155 and for one asset in source 156; the released targets apply it to each kind of property independently, with a $300 EV ceiling.

by_task.when: An asset is considered under 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3).
by_task.procedure: First require that it be one of the listed household-use categories, then assign no more than the lesser of its value and the $700 per-item limit. Evaluate jewelry separately under § 522(d)(4).
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use the $14,875 aggregate ceiling as the claim for one item, and do not classify jewelry under § 522(d)(3) merely because it is held for personal or household use.

operations.rationale: Source 154 EV contained an extra § 522(d)(3) claim for jewelry, while source 155 EV assigned $4,300 to a single household item despite the statute's $700 particular-item ceiling. This distinct correction removes the wrong legal category and fixes the wrong amount without disturbing valid § 522(d)(3) selections.

by_task.when: Arizona law applies and the facts identify an item as medically or professionally prescribed assistive equipment for the debtor or a dependent.
by_task.procedure: Treat the item as a prescribed prosthetic or mobility aid under Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(9) and claim its full value because the supplied provision states no dollar cap.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify prescribed assistive equipment as ordinary household furniture merely because it is used in the home; do not apply this rule to ordinary furniture lacking the prescription or assistive condition.

operations.rationale: In source 152 EV, the parent selected the household-furnishings provision for the medically prescribed assistive item, producing one false positive and omitting § 33-1125(9). The same-case EC answer and released EV target confirm the prescribed-aid classification; the unrelated household furnishing remains under § 33-1123.
